title.zh: 卷七十九下 儒林列傳
title.raw: 卷七十九下 儒林列傳 Volume 79b: Biographies of Confucian Scholars 2

title.zh: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子
title.raw: 卷五十三 列傳第二十三 愍懷太子 Volume 53 Biographies 23: Crown Prince Minhuai

title.zh: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登
title.en: Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng
title.raw: 卷一百一十五 載記第十五 苻丕 苻登 Volume 115 Records 15: Fu Pi; Fu Deng

value.zh: 《前書》魯人申公受《詩》於浮丘伯，為作詁訓，是為《魯詩》；
value.en: The Han shu records that Shen Gong of Lu studied the Odes under Fuqiu Bo and compiled glosses—what became the Lu school of the classic.
value.literal: The Former Documents: Shen Gong of Lu received the Odes from Fuqiu Bo, for them made gloss and exegesis, and this is the 'Odes in the Lu tradition';

value.zh: 齊人轅固生亦傳《詩》，是為《齊詩》；
value.en: Yuan Gu of Qi handed down another line—the Qi Odes.
value.literal: Yuan Gu of Qi likewise transmitted the Odes, and this is the 'Odes in the Qi tradition';

value.zh: 燕人韓嬰亦傳《詩》，是為《韓詩》；
value.en: Han Ying of Yan founded the Han school of the Odes.
value.literal: Han Ying of Yan likewise transmitted the Odes, and this is the 'Odes in the Han tradition';

value.zh: 三家皆立博士。
value.en: All three received chairs at the imperial academy.
value.literal: All three houses had Erudites established.

value.zh: 趙人毛萇傳《詩》，是為《毛詩》，未得立。
value.en: Mao Chang of Zhao taught what became the Mao commentary, which had no doctoral chair in Western Han.
value.literal: Mao Chang of Zhao transmitted the Odes, and this is the 'Mao Odes'; it did not obtain establishment.

value.zh: 太傅陳蕃辟之，與參政事。
value.en: Grand Tutor Chen Fan brought him into government.
value.literal: Grand Tutor Chen Fan summoned him to join in governance.

value.zh: 蕃敗，休坐廢錮，乃作《春秋公羊解詁》，覃思不窺門，十有七年。
value.en: When Chen Fan fell, He Xiu was banned from office and spent seventeen years indoors writing his Gongyang gloss.
value.literal: When Fan was defeated, Xiu sat in dismissal and prohibition from office; thereupon he composed Glosses on the Gongyang Spring and Autumn, pondering so deeply that he did not peer out his gate for seventeen years.

value.zh: 又注訓《孝經》、《論語》、風角七分，皆經緯典謨，不與守文同說。
value.en: He also glossed the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and wind-omen lore, aiming at classical models rather than narrow literalism.
value.literal: Further he annotated and glossed the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, and wind-horn seven parts, all patterned on canonical models and not the same as pedants who cling to the letter.

value.zh: 又以《春秋》駁漢事六百餘條，妙得《公羊》本意。
value.en: He used Gongyang to critique over six hundred Han precedents, capturing the school's core intent.
value.literal: Further by the Spring and Autumn he refuted more than six hundred items in Han affairs, subtly obtaining the original intent of Gongyang.

value.zh: 休善曆算，與其師博士羊弼，追述李育意以難二傳，作《公羊墨守》、《左氏膏肓》、《穀梁廢疾》。
value.en: With his teacher Erudite Yang Bi he developed Li Yu's attacks on the Zuo and Guliang schools in three famous polemics.
value.literal: Xiu was good at calendrical calculation; together with his teacher the Erudite Yang Bi he pursued and stated Li Yu's ideas to object to the two traditions, composing Gongyang Ink-Bound, Zuo Ailing, and Guliang Morbid.

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 苻丕 苻登
value.en: This chapter records Fu Pi and Fu Deng.
value.literal: Fu Pi; Fu Deng.

value.zh: 是時安西呂光自西域還師，至於宜禾，堅涼州刺史梁熙謀閉境距之。
value.en: Meanwhile Lü Guang, general who pacifies the west, was marching home from the Western Regions and had reached Yihe; Liang Xi, inspector of Liangzhou under Fu Jian, meant to shut the frontier and block his entry.
value.literal: At this time the General Who Pacifies the West Lü Guang was returning his army from the Western Regions and reached Yihe; Liang Xi, Fu Jian's Inspector of Liangzhou, planned to close the border and keep him out.

value.zh: 高昌太守楊翰言於熙曰：「呂光新定西國，兵強氣銳，其鋒不可當也。
value.en: Yang Han, administrator of Gaochang, warned Liang Xi: "Lü Guang has just brought the west under his hand; his soldiers are fresh and fierce, and nothing can stand in the path of his thrust.
value.literal: The Administrator of Gaochang Yang Han spoke to Xi, saying: "Lü Guang has newly subdued the western lands; his troops are strong and his morale keen, and the edge of his advance cannot be withstood.

value.zh: 度其事意，必有異圖。
value.en: Judging from how things are moving, he must be nursing ambitions beyond a simple homecoming.
value.literal: Considering the drift of events, he is sure to harbor other designs.

value.zh: 且今關中擾亂，京師存亡未知，自河已西迄於流沙，地方萬里，帶甲十萬，鼎峙之勢實在今日。
value.en: Moreover Guanzhong is chaos and the fate of the capital uncertain; west of the Yellow River stretches ten thousand li of ground to the desert's edge, garrisoned by a hundred thousand men—if ever there was a moment for contending powers to face one another, it is this.
value.literal: Moreover the Guanzhong is in turmoil, and whether the capital survives is unknown; from the Yellow River westward to the shifting sands, the territory is ten thousand li, with a hundred thousand armored men—the time for a tripartite standoff is truly now.

value.zh: 若光出流沙，其勢難測。
value.en: Once Lü Guang breaks out of the western wastes, no one can tell what he will do next.
value.literal: If Lü Guang emerges from the desert, his movements will be hard to predict.

value.zh: 高梧穀口，水險之要，宜先守之而奪其水。
value.en: Gaowu Gorge is a defile where water and ground favor the defender; hold it first and deny him water.
value.literal: Gaowu Gorge is a choke point of water and terrain; you should seize it first and cut off his water supply.

value.zh: 彼既窮渴，自然投戈。
value.en: Thirst and exhaustion will do your work for you—they will throw down their arms of their own accord.
value.literal: When they are exhausted and parched, they will naturally cast aside their weapons.

value.zh: 如其以遠不守，伊吾之關亦可距也。
value.en: Even if he scorns to contest that distant ground, the Yiwu barrier can still block him.
value.literal: If he disdains to hold that distant line, the pass at Yiwu can still bar him.

value.zh: 若度此二要，雖有子房之策，難為計矣。
value.en: Let him through both choke points, and not even Zhang Liang's cunning could save your position.
value.literal: If he passes these two critical points, even with a Zhang Liang's stratagems you will find no remedy.

value.zh: 地有所必爭，真此機也。」
value.en: Some ground must be contested at any cost; the opportunity is now."
value.literal: There are positions that must be fought for—this is the moment."

value.zh: 熙弗從。
value.en: Liang Xi refused to listen.
value.literal: Xi did not follow this advice.

value.zh: 美水令犍為張統說熙曰：「主上傾國南討，覆敗而還。
value.en: Zhang Tong of Qianwei, magistrate of Meishui, said to Liang Xi: "Our lord emptied the kingdom for a southern campaign and returned in defeat.
value.literal: The magistrate of Meishui, Zhang Tong of Qianwei, urged Xi, saying: "The sovereign raised the whole realm for a southern expedition and came back in ruin.

value.zh: 慕容垂擅兵河北，泓、沖寇逼京師，丁零雜虜，跋扈關、洛，州郡奸豪，所在風扇，王綱弛絕，人懷利己。
value.en: Murong Chui holds the Hebei plain; Murong Hong and Murong Chong threaten the capital; Dingling and other tribes rampage through Guanzhong and the Luoyang region; local magnates everywhere take the cue to rebel; imperial authority frays and every hand reaches for advantage.
value.literal: Murong Chui wields arms north of the Yellow River; Hong and Chong press the capital; Dingling and mixed barbarians run riot in Guan and Luo; unscrupulous strongmen in every province rise like windblown grass; the royal net hangs slack and each man seeks his private gain.

value.zh: 今呂光回師，將軍何以抗也？」
value.en: Lü Guang is marching home at the head of a seasoned host—how do you mean to stop him?"
value.literal: Now Lü Guang is leading his army back—how will you, General, resist him?"

value.zh: 熙曰：「誠深憂之，未知計之所出。」
value.en: Liang Xi answered, "The danger weighs on me, yet I see no clear course."
value.literal: Xi said: "I am deeply troubled, but I do not know what plan to adopt."

value.zh: 統曰：「光雄果勇毅，明略絕人，今以蕩西域之威，擁歸師之銳，鋒若猛火之盛于原，弗可敵也。
value.en: Zhang Tong replied, "Lü Guang is a fighter of rare courage and cunning; fresh from conquering the west and leading veterans homeward, he strikes like wildfire across dry grass—you cannot meet him head-on.
value.literal: Tong said: "Lü Guang is bold, resolute, and brave beyond ordinary men; now, with the prestige of having swept the Western Regions and the keen edge of a homecoming army, his spearhead is like a fierce fire racing across the plain—he cannot be opposed.

value.zh: 將軍世受殊恩，忠誠夙著，立勳王室，宜在於今。
value.en: Your family has enjoyed extraordinary grace, your devotion has never been in doubt, and you have served the throne with distinction—now is the hour to prove it again.
value.literal: The General's house has received singular favor for generations, your loyalty has long been manifest, and you have raised achievements for the royal house—this is the moment to show it.

value.zh: 行唐公洛，上之從弟，勇冠一時。
value.en: The duke of Xingtang, Fu Luo, is the emperor's cousin on the father's side and the foremost warrior of his day.
value.literal: The Duke of Xingtang, Luo, is His Majesty's younger cousin by the same grandfather; his valor is unmatched in the age.

value.zh: 為將軍計者，莫若奉為盟主，以攝眾望，推忠義以總率群豪，則光無異心也。
value.en: The wise course is to recognize Fu Luo as leader of the alliance and win the people's hope, then gather the heroes under the banner of duty—so Lü Guang finds no opening for disloyalty.
value.literal: For the General's planning, nothing would be better than to acknowledge him as covenant lord to gather popular expectation, and to rally the bold with loyalty and righteousness—then Lü Guang will have no separate ambition.

value.zh: 資其精銳，東兼毛興，連王統、楊璧，集四州之眾，掃凶逆于諸夏，甯帝室於關中，此桓文之舉也。」
value.en: Use his elite columns to drive east, link with Mao Xing, Wang Tong, and Yang Bi, combine the armies of four provinces, clear the heartland of traitors, and set the dynasty right in Guanzhong—work worthy of Duke Huan or Duke Wen."
value.literal: With his picked troops strike east to absorb Mao Xing, join Wang Tong and Yang Bi, assemble the hosts of four provinces, sweep the rebels from the central plains, and restore the imperial house in Guanzhong—this is the deed of a Huan or a Wen."

value.zh: 熙又不從。
value.en: Liang Xi still would not take the advice.
value.literal: Again Xi did not follow.

value.zh: 殺洛於西海，以子胤為鷹揚將軍，率眾五萬距光於酒泉。
value.en: Instead he executed Fu Luo at Xihai, named his son Yin general who spreads might, and sent fifty thousand soldiers to block Lü Guang at Jiuquan.
value.literal: He killed Luo at Xihai, appointed his son Yin General Who Spreads Might, and led fifty thousand men to oppose Lü Guang at Jiuquan.

value.zh: 敦煌太守姚靜、晉昌太守李純以郡降光。
value.en: Yao Jing of Dunhuang and Li Chun of Jinchang yielded their prefectures to Lü Guang.
value.literal: The Administrator of Dunhuang Yao Jing and the Administrator of Jinchang Li Chun surrendered their commanderies to Lü Guang.

value.zh: 胤及光戰于安彌，為光所敗。
value.en: Fu Yin met Lü Guang at Anmi and was routed.
value.literal: Yin fought Lü Guang at Anmi and was defeated by him.

value.zh: 武威太守彭濟執熙迎光，光殺之。
value.en: Peng Ji, administrator of Wuwei, took Liang Xi prisoner and opened the gates to Lü Guang, who then put Liang Xi to death.
value.literal: The Administrator of Wuwei Peng Ji seized Xi and welcomed Lü Guang; Lü Guang killed Xi.

value.zh: 建威、西郡太守索泮，奮威、督洪池已南諸軍事、酒泉太守宋皓等，並為光所殺。
value.en: Suo Pan, who held Jianwei and the western commandery, Song Hao of Jiuquan—who served as general who rouses might and directed troops south of Hongchi—and others likewise fell to Lü Guang's blade.
value.literal: Suo Pan, administrator of Jianwei and Xijun, and Song Hao, administrator of Jiuquan who held the office of general who rouses might and supervised military affairs south of Hongchi Pool, together with others, were all killed by Lü Guang.

value.zh: 堅尚書令、魏昌公苻纂自關中來奔，拜太尉，進封東海王。
value.en: Fu Zuan, Fu Jian's director of the secretariat and duke of Weichang, arrived as a refugee from Guanzhong; Fu Pi named him grand commandant and raised him to prince of Donghai.
value.literal: Fu Jian's Director of the Secretariat and Duke of Weichang Fu Zuan came fleeing from Guanzhong and was appointed Grand Commandant, advanced to Prince of Donghai.

value.zh: 以中山太守王兗為平東將軍、平州刺史、阜城侯，苻定為征東將軍、冀州牧、高城侯，苻紹為鎮東將軍、督冀州諸軍事、重合侯，苻謨為征西將軍、幽州牧、高邑侯，苻亮為鎮北大將軍、督幽、并二州諸軍事，並進爵郡公。
value.en: Wang Yan of Zhongshan became general who pacifies the east, inspector of Pingzhou, and marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding general who conquers the east, governor of Jizhou, and marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao general who guards the east, with overall command in Jizhou, and marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo general who conquers the west, governor of Youzhou, and marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang general who guards the north, with joint authority over You and Bing—all were promoted to commandery dukes.
value.literal: He made the Administrator of Zhongshan Wang Yan General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Pingzhou, and Marquis of Fucheng; Fu Ding General Who Conquers the East, Governor of Jizhou, and Marquis of Gaocheng; Fu Shao General Who Guards the East, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Jizhou, and Marquis of Chonghe; Fu Mo General Who Conquers the West, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Gaoyi; Fu Liang General Who Guards the North, Commander of Military Affairs in You and Bing, and all were advanced in noble rank to Dukes of commanderies.

value.zh: 定、紹據信都，謨、亮先據常山，慕容垂之圍鄴城也，並降于垂，聞丕稱尊號，遣使謝罪。
value.en: Fu Ding and Fu Shao held Xindu while Fu Mo and Fu Liang had seized Changshan first; both pairs had gone over to Murong Chui when he invested Ye, yet when Fu Pi declared himself emperor they dispatched messengers begging forgiveness.
value.literal: Ding and Shao held Xindu; Mo and Liang had first occupied Changshan; when Murong Chui besieged Ye they had both surrendered to Chui, but on hearing that Fu Pi had assumed the imperial title they sent envoys to apologize.

value.zh: 王兗固守博陵，與垂相持。
value.en: Wang Yan shut himself in Boling and held the line against Murong Chui.
value.literal: Wang Yan stubbornly defended Boling against Chui.

value.zh: 左將軍竇沖、秦州刺史王統、河州刺史毛興、益州刺史王廣、南秦州刺史楊璧、衛將軍楊定，並據隴右，遣使招丕，請討姚萇。
value.en: Dou Chong, general of the left; Wang Tong, inspector of Qinzhou; Mao Xing, inspector of Hezhou; Wang Guang, inspector of Yizhou; Yang Bi, inspector of south Qinzhou; and Yang Ding, general of the guards, each held ground in Longyou and wrote to Fu Pi offering to strike Yao Chang.
value.literal: The General of the Left Dou Chong, the Inspector of Qinzhou Wang Tong, the Inspector of Hezhou Mao Xing, the Inspector of Yizhou Wang Guang, the Inspector of South Qinzhou Yang Bi, and the General of the Guards Yang Ding all held Longyou and sent envoys to summon Fu Pi, asking to campaign against Yao Chang.

value.zh: 丕大悅，以定為驃騎大將軍、雍州牧，沖為征西大將軍、梁州牧，統鎮西大將軍，興車騎大將軍，璧征南大將軍，並開府儀同三司，加散騎常侍，廣安西將軍，皆進位州牧。
value.en: Fu Pi was delighted: Yang Ding became grand general of agile cavalry and governor of Yongzhou; Dou Chong grand general who conquers the west and governor of Liangzhou; Wang Tong grand general who guards the west; Mao Xing grand general of chariots and cavalry; Yang Bi grand general who conquers the south—each with an independent headquarters and honors matching the three dukes, plus the title cavalier attendant-in-ordinary; Wang Guang became general who pacifies the west; all were raised to governorships.
value.literal: Fu Pi was greatly pleased; he made Yang Ding Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Yongzhou, Chong Grand General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liangzhou, Tong Grand General Who Guards the West, Xing Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bi Grand General Who Conquers the South, all with the privilege of opening a general's office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Guang General Who Pacifies the West, all advanced to the position of provincial governor.

value.zh: 登以竇沖為車騎大將軍、南秦州牧，楊定為大將軍、益州牧，楊璧為司空、梁州牧。
value.en: Fu Deng named Dou Chong grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of south Qinzhou, Yang Ding grand general and governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi minister of works and governor of Liangzhou.
value.literal: Deng made Dou Chong Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of South Qinzhou, Yang Ding Grand General and Governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou.

value.zh: 登收合餘兵，退據胡空堡，遣使齎書加竇沖大司馬、驃騎將軍、前鋒大都督、都督隴東諸軍事，楊定左丞相、上大將軍、都督中外諸軍事，楊璧大將軍、都督隴右諸軍事。
value.en: Fu Deng regrouped at Hu Kong's fort and promoted Dou Chong to grand marshal and Yang Ding to left chancellor with full military authority, Yang Bi to grand general over Longyou.
value.literal: Deng gathered the remaining troops, withdrew to occupy Hu Kong's fort, sent envoys bearing documents to advance Dou Chong to Grand Marshal, General of Agile Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Longdong, Yang Ding to Left Chancellor, Supreme Grand General, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Yang Bi to Grand General, Supervisor of Military Affairs in Longyou.

value.zh: 遣沖率見眾為先驅，自繁川趣長安。
value.en: Dou Chong led the van toward Chang'an from Fanchuan.
value.literal: He dispatched Chong to lead the troops at hand as vanguard, himself going from Fanchuan toward Chang'an.

value.zh: 登率眾從新平逕據新豐之千戶固。
value.en: Fu Deng cut through Xinping and seized Qianhu fort at Xinfeng.
value.literal: Deng led the host from Xinping by a direct route to occupy Qianhu Fort of Xinfeng.

value.zh: 使定率隴上諸軍為其後繼，璧留守仇池。
value.en: Yang Ding was to follow with the Long uplands levies; Yang Bi stayed to hold Qiuqi.
value.literal: He ordered Ding to lead the various armies on Longshang as his rear support, while Bi remained to guard Qiuqi.

value.zh: 又命其并州刺史楊政、冀州刺史楊楷率所統大會長安。
value.en: Yang Zheng of Bingzhou and Yang Kai of Jizhou were to march on Chang'an for the general muster.
value.literal: He also ordered his Inspector of Bingzhou Yang Zheng and Inspector of Jizhou Yang Kai to lead their commands in a great rendezvous at Chang'an.

value.zh: 萇遣其將軍王破虜略地秦州，楊定及破虜戰于清水之格奴阪，大敗之。
value.en: Yao Chang's Wang Polu raided Qinzhou until Yang Ding shattered him at Genu Ford on the Qingshui.
value.literal: Chang sent his general Wang Polu to seize territory in Qinzhou; Yang Ding and Polu fought at Genu Slope on the Qingshui, and Ding inflicted a great defeat on him.

value.zh: 登攻張龍世於鴦泉堡，姚萇救之，登引退。
value.en: Fu Deng besieged Zhang Longshi at Yuanquan until Yao Chang relieved him, forcing Fu Deng to pull back.
value.literal: Deng attacked Zhang Longshi at Yuanquan Fort; Yao Chang came to save him, and Deng led a withdrawal.

value.zh: 萇密遣其將任瓫、宗度詐為內應，遣使招登，許開門納之。
value.en: Yao Chang secretly ordered Ren Chong and Zong Du to feign treason and invite Fu Deng inside the walls.
value.literal: Chang secretly sent his generals Ren Chong and Zong Du to pretend to be inner collaborators, dispatched envoys to summon Deng, promising to open the gates and admit him.

value.zh: 登以為然。
value.en: Fu Deng believed the ruse.
value.literal: Deng believed it was so.

value.zh: 雷惡地馳謂登曰：「姚萇多計略，善御人，必為奸變，願深宜詳思。」
value.en: Lei Edi galloped up to warn him: "Yao Chang is cunning and knows how to bind men—he will betray you; think twice."
value.literal: Lei Edi rode in haste and said to Deng: "Yao Chang is full of stratagems and skilled at controlling men; he is sure to work a treacherous turn—I pray you think it through most carefully."

value.zh: 登乃止。
value.en: Fu Deng called off the attempt.
value.literal: Deng thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 萇聞惡地之詣登也，謂諸將曰：「此羌多奸智，今其詣登，事必無成。」
value.en: Yao Chang told his officers, "That Qiang is sly; now that he has warned Fu Deng, the trap is sprung for nothing."
value.literal: When Chang heard that Edi had gone to Deng, he said to his generals: "This Qiang is full of treacherous cleverness; now that he has gone to Deng, the affair is sure not to succeed."

value.zh: 登聞萇懸門以待之，大驚，謂左右曰：「雷征東其殆聖乎！
value.en: Learning that Yao Chang had lifted the portcullis in ambush, Fu Deng gasped to his staff, "Lei the east-conquering general must be clairvoyant!
value.literal: Deng heard that Chang had raised the drawbridge to await him, was greatly startled, and said to those at his side: "Lei, General Who Conquers the East, is perhaps a sage!

value.zh: 微此公，朕幾為豎子所誤。」
value.en: Without him I would have walked into that boy's snare."
value.literal: Without this lord, I would almost have been misled by the stripling."

value.zh: 萇攻陷新羅堡。
value.en: Yao Chang then took Xinluo fort.
value.literal: Chang attacked and captured Xinluo Fort.

value.zh: 萇撫風太守齊益男奔登。
value.en: Qi Yinan, governor of Fufeng under Yao Chang, defected to Fu Deng.
value.literal: Chang's Administrator of Fufeng Qi Yinan fled to Deng.

value.zh: 登將軍路柴、強武等並以眾降於萇。
value.en: Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and other Fu Deng commanders went over to Yao Chang with their troops.
value.literal: Fu Deng's generals Lu Chai, Qiang Wu, and others all led their hosts to surrender to Chang.

value.zh: 登攻萇將張業生於隴東，萇救之，不克而退。
value.en: Fu Deng struck Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Yao Chang tried to help but retired without breaking the siege.
value.literal: Deng attacked Chang's general Zhang Yesheng in Longdong; Chang came to his rescue, could not overcome him, and withdrew.

value.zh: 登將軍魏褐飛攻姚當成於杏城，為萇所殺。
value.en: Wei Hefei besieged Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and died at Yao Chang's hand.
value.literal: Fu Deng's general Wei Hefei attacked Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng and was killed by Chang.
